subject: Registrations open- BCC(Business Case Challenge)
body:
Greetings from AIESEC in Patiala,

We are excited to introduce the Business Case Challenge (BCC) — an
immersive overnight hackathon designed for college students eager to test
their creativity, strategic thinking, and problem-solving skills in
real-world business situations.

Participants will compete in teams of 3–5 members, working through the
night to dissect an industry-based case, generate innovative solutions, and
develop actionable strategies under time constraints. With mentors

subject: Fwd: FW: Hiring Aspiring Candidates – Join Us for Buddy Program
body:
Dear Sir/Madam

I hope this email finds you well.

I'm writing on behalf of HackCulture, a global community that empowers
students and professionals to build innovative products through hackathons
and real-world challenges. We’re reaching out to invite your esteemed
institution to nominate students for the HackCulture Buddy Program — our
Campus Ambassador initiative.

This program is designed to provide leadership, mentorship, and hands-on
experience to selected students, enabling them to play a pivotal role in
hosting and supporting HackCulture hackathons and events. We believe your
students would greatly benefit from this opportunity to become leaders,
mentors, and community builders.

We are currently looking to onboard *1 to 3 enthusiastic students*
(preferably from 1st or 2nd year) who can act as *Hackathon Buddies* –
serving as ambassadors who’ll help us stay connected with your college,
coordinate participation, and share important updates.

If possible, we would appreciate it if you could:

   - Share this opportunity directly with interested students, or
   - Circulate the following form among eligible students:

We truly value the contributions of leading institutions like yours and

candidates. Kindly let us know if you’d prefer a call to discuss this in

subject: Instructions for Students (MST, September -2026)
body:
THAPAR INSTITUTE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY: PATIALA

   (Declared as Deemed-to-be-University u/s 3 of the UGC Act, 1956)

*Instructions to Students for Mid Semester Test (MST)*

1.*There will be a complete frisking of the students before the entry into
the examination centre, so the students are instructed to reach their
respective examination centre atleast 30 minutes before the start of the
examination in their respective session.*

2. *Mobile phones, digital smart watches/devices and any other
un-authorized material are strictly banned in the examination centre. If
caught, these will be returned by the office of COE after the completion of
the last MST and action will be taken as per TIET Academic Regulations on
Unfair Means Cases.*

3. *Students are NOT allowed to carry books/bags/wallets inside the
examination area.  The bags should strictly be kept outside the examination
area.*

4.    The students are required to be seated at their respective seats 10
minutes before the start of the examination. *There are three sessions for
MST i.e., 9:00 am, 1.00 am and 4:30 pm. Each session will be of 2 hours’
duration.*

5. *Students will NOT be allowed to appear in the examination
without ORIGINAL IDENTITY CARD  of TIET.*

6. Students will *NOT* be allowed to enter the examination hall 10 minutes
after the start of the examination.

7. *Students have to bring their own transparent water bottle.*

8.The detailed seating plan will be displayed at the entrance of each
examination room. However, students are advised to check their respective exam
portal (exams.thapar.edu) for the block/room in which the seat is allocated
to them to appear in the examination.

9.   The transfer/exchange of items such as calculators, pencils, scales,
etc. is strictly prohibited during the examination. The students should
carry their own items for use.

10.     Students found copying or indulging in any unfair means will be
dealt with as per the TIET rules on unfair means. If any student is
suspected by the invigilator or any authorized person of having resorted to
unfair means, his/her answer book shall be seized. The papers or any
materials duly signed by the invigilator and Superintendent, found in
possession of the student shall be stitched with his/her answer book in his
presence.  The Superintendent shall ask the candidate to make a statement
in writing, explaining his/her conduct.  In case the candidate refuses to
do so, the fact of his/her refusal should be recorded by the
Superintendent, which should be attested by atleast one invigilator on
duty. Second answer-sheet will be issued to the student and will be sent
along with the first answer sheet in a sealed envelope.

11. Any student wishing to leave the examination is allowed to do so only
after 1 hour of the start of Examination.

12. Students will *NOT* be allowed to move from his/her seat for water,
washroom, etc. during the examination, except in unavoidable circumstances,
with the due permission of invigilator(s).

Regards
Prof. Naveen Kwatra
Controller of Examination
Professor, Department of Civil Engineering
Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology

subject: Instructions for Students of UG-I (MST, Oct, 2024)
body:
THAPAR INSTITUTE OF ENGINEERING & TECHNOLOGY: PATIALA

(Declared as Deemed-to-be-University u/s 3 of the UGC Act, 1956)
 *Instructions to Students for Mid Semester Test (MST)*

1.        *There will be a complete frisking of the students before the
entry into the examination centre, so the students are instructed to reach
their respective examination centre atleast 45 minutes before the start of
the examination in their respective session.*

2.    *Mobile phones, digital smart watches/devices and any other
un-authorized material are strictly banned in the examination centre. If
caught, these will be returned by the office of COE after the completion of
the last MST and action will be taken as per TIET Academic Regulations on
Unfair Means Cases.*

*Students are also instructed not to bring any wallets inside the
examination hall.*

*3.  Students will NOT be allowed to appear in the examination without both
of the following documents:*

*     (i)    Admission letter issued by TIET*

*  (ii)   **Any proof of identity issued by Govt. of India i.e.,
AADHAAR CARD, PASSPORT, DRIVING LICENSE etc.*

*         If a student fails to provide both of the above documents, the
student will not be allowed to appear for the exam. *

4.        *Students are NOT allowed to carry books/bags inside the
examination area.  The bags should strictly be kept outside the examination
area. Students are advised not to keep any money / expensive items in the
bag while keeping it outside the examination hall.  *

5.     The students are required to be seated at their respective seats 10
minutes before the start of the examination. *There is one session for MST
i.e., 4:30 - 6:30 pm (except for the course of 'Engineering Drawing' which
will be held in three sessions as per the time given in the webkiosk of the
respective student). *

*Each session of MST will be of 2 hours duration.*

6.             Students will *NOT* be allowed to enter the examination hall
10 minutes after the start of the examination. If a student reports to the
examination centre 10 minutes after the start of the exam, due to some
unavoidable circumstances, he/she will give a written explanation for being
late to the COE/Centre Supdt/ Deputy Supdt.

7.             *Students have to bring their own transparent water bottle.*

8.       The detailed seating plan will be displayed at the entrance of
each examination room. However, students are advised to check their
respective webkiosk for the block/room in which the seat is allocated to
them to appear in the examination.

9.   The transfer/exchange of items such as calculators, pencils, scales,
etc. is strictly prohibited during the examination. The students should
carry their own items for use.

10.     Students found copying or indulging in any unfair means will be
dealt with as per the TIET rules on unfair means. *TIET has ZERO tolerance
for students using unfair means in examinations.* If any student is
suspected by the invigilator or any authorized person of having resorted to
unfair means, his/her answer book shall be seized. The papers or any
materials duly signed by the invigilator and Superintendent, found in
possession of the student shall be stitched with his/her answer book in his
presence.  The Superintendent shall ask the candidate to make a statement
in writing, explaining his/her conduct.  In case the candidate refuses to
do so, the fact of his/her refusal should be recorded by the
Superintendent, which should be attested by atleast one invigilator on
duty. Second answer-sheet will be issued to the student and will be sent
along with the first answer sheet in a sealed envelope.

11.        Any student wishing to leave the examination is allowed to do so
only after 1 hour of the start of Examination.

12.    Students will *NOT* be allowed to move from his/her seat for water,
washroom, etc. during the examination, except in unavoidable circumstances,
and that too with the due permission of invigilator(s).

Sd/-

(Controller of Examination)

Regards
Dr. S. S. Bhatia
Controller of Examination,
Professor, Department of Mathematics,
Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology,
Patiala-147004, Punjab, India.

body:
We hope this message finds you in good health and spirits. This is
regarding the announcement of *Cohort 8 of the India Semiconductor
Workforce Development Program (ISWDP), *run by the* Indian Institute of
Science (IISc) Bangalore, *in collaboration with* Synopsys Inc., USA,
*and* Samsung
Semiconductor India Research (SSIR)*. ISWDP is a program tailored to bridge
the process technology and device design skill gap in the swiftly expanding
semiconductor sector through a meticulously designed course
<https://iisc-iswdp.org/index.php>, covering the foundational and advanced
concepts, also offering a hands-on approach through microelectronics lab
experience.

The live virtual program comprises four levels, i.e., Level 1, Level 2,
Advance, and Custom. Launched in March 2024, the program runs 4 cohorts
throughout the year. Following the successful completion of 6 cohorts with
around 4000 participants and the current progress of Cohort 7, we are happy
to announce that registrations are now open for Cohort 8 starting *June 1,
2026*.

*May we request your office to kindly disseminate this information to
students and faculties of the concerned departments in your institute by
forwarding this email and posting it on respective notice boards?*

*How to enrol?*

   - *Samsung Fellowship: *Students can *fill up the Google Form *
   https://forms.gle/EzsuxnKtWCnbjGG86 by *May 3, **𝟐𝟎𝟐**6, **𝟓* *𝐏𝐌*,
   to register through the Samsung Fellowship, more details of which can be
   found here https://iisc-iswdp.org/scholarship.php. We encourage
   meritorious students to register through this route.

   - *Direct Registration:* Alternatively, students can simply click on
   this link for direct registration:
   https://iswdp.registeryourseat.in/index.php.

Please note that the slots in each cohort are limited, so prompt action is
advisable.

We hope your colleagues and students make the best use of this effort from
IISc, Synopsys, and Samsung Semiconductor India Research. Please do not
hesitate to reach out to us in case of questions. We will be regularly
posting program schedules and other important updates on our LinkedIn page.
Those interested in the program can follow us on LinkedIn at
https://www.linkedin.com/company/iswdp/

subject: Register for the JETRO Regional Internship Fair on 7th Aug 2026 – Meet Leading Japanese Companies at TIET
body:
Dear Students,

We are pleased to invite you to participate in the *JETRO Regional
Internship Fair 2026*, an exclusive opportunity to engage directly with
leading Japanese companies visiting our campus.

As Japan continues to face a growing demand for highly skilled global
talent, an increasing number of Japanese companies are actively exploring
long-term talent pathways with India. The JETRO Regional Internship Fair
has been conceptualized as the beginning of a long-term engagement between
Japanese industry and Indian higher education institutions, creating
meaningful opportunities for student mobility, internships, employment, and
academic collaboration

This programme has been designed to introduce students to Japan's industry
landscape while creating opportunities for future internships, careers, and
international collaboration. Many of the participating companies are
visiting India for the first time and are eager to meet talented students,
understand India's academic ecosystem, and explore future engagement with
Indian universities.

For your reference, we have attached a brief overview of each participating
company. While the profiles provide an introduction to their work and areas
of interest*, we understand that there may be questions requiring
additional clarity on details of the proposed internship duration/FTE,

Doctoral applicants: No older than 40 years old

subject: Reg: Compulsory Proficiency Test.
body:
Dear Students,

It has been observed that students often face considerable uncertainty
while making career decisions at the beginning of their third year of
undergraduate study. This is understandable, as engineering students have
multiple career pathways and opportunities to choose from after completing
their degree.

To help you make informed and well-aligned career decisions, the *Centre
for Training & Development (CTD)* is conducting a *Mandatory Career
Assessment Drive* for *BE 3rd-Year Students (All Branches)*.

The assessment is designed to help you understand your strengths,
interests, personality traits, motivations, and suitability across various
career domains.
The Career Assessment will comprise:

   -

   *Strategically Designed Proficiency Test:* An online MCQ-based
   assessment covering *aptitude, work personality, interests, and career
   motivations*.
   -

   *Detailed Assessment Report:* A comprehensive report featuring
   statistically generated scores and coefficients that reflect your
   proficiency and suitability across different career domains.
   -

   *Personalized Career Counselling:* Individualized guidance based on your
   assessment report, including insights into suitable career pathways and
   strategies for preparing for future academic and professional challenges.

Important Details

   -

   *Eligible Students:* BE 3rd-Year Students – *All Branches*
   -

   *Mode:* Online
   -

   *Test Window:* *October 08 to October 25, 2026*
   -

   *Assessment Link:* To be shared from [EMAIL]

Important Notice

The *Career Assessment is COMPULSORY for all BE 3rd-Year students (all
branches)*. Completion of the assessment is *mandatory from an
employability and career-readiness perspective*.

Students are therefore advised to complete the assessment within the
stipulated timeline and make the most of this opportunity to gain greater
clarity about their career aspirations and future professional journey.

*Your career begins with the right understanding of yourself. Make the
assessment count!*

subject: Advisory Regarding Unauthorized Promotion of Events on Social Media
body:
*CIRCULAR *

It has come to the notice of the Institute that *02** students of the
3rd/4th Year and 01 student of the 1st Year have been using their personal
social media/Instagram accounts to create, post, and promote content
relating to a Fresher Party being organized outside the TIET premises. It
has been observed that the mentioned students created their social media
posts with the intention of influencing and encouraging first-year students
to participate in such events. *

*The Institute has taken serious note of this, the use of Institute
premises and the student community for the personal promotion and benefit
of events that are neither organized nor approved by the Institute. The
Institute has taken strict disciplinary action against the three students
concerned.* *They have been directed to submit written apologies, and
necessary disciplinary action has been initiated/taken against them in
accordance with the applicable Institute rules and regulations.*

In this regard, all students are hereby strictly advised to: *Refrain from
promotion of any event or activity that is not organized, approved, or
endorsed by the Institute.*

This circular may be treated as an official advisory to all students.

Dr. Meenakshi Rana
Dean of Student Affairs
Professor, Department of Mathematics
Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology

Dear Sir/Madam,

I hope this message finds you well. I am inviting applications from highly
motivated candidates for the position of Junior Research Fellow (JRF) in
two exciting projects funded by the Telecom Centers of Excellence,
Department of Telecommunications:

1.     *Zero Touch Realization of Decentralized Federated Learning for
Real-Time Applications in 6G Assisted Edge Networks* (Project Code: 119)

2.     *Artificial Intelligence for Supporting Integrated Sensing and
Secured Communication in 6G Assisted Edge Networks* (Project Code: 309)

*Eligibility Criteria:*

*Educational Qualification:*

M.Tech./M.E./M.S./BS-MS in Computer Science/Communication/Artificial
Intelligence/Electronics and Communication Engineering or related areas
with a minimum CPI of 6.5 and a valid GATE score (within the last five
years).

OR

B.Tech./B.E. in Computer Science and
Engineering/Electrical/Electronics/Communication/Instrumentation with a
minimum CPI of 6.5 and a valid GATE score.

*GATE Score Exemption:*

Candidates with B.Tech. degree from IITs/IISc/IISERs with a minimum CPI of
8.0 are exempted from GATE requirements.

*Desirable Qualifications:*

Prior working/research experience in Communication, Networking, Security,
or Machine Learning will be given preference.

*Fellowship Amount:*

Rs. 37,000 + HRA per month for the first two years

Rs. 42,000 + HRA per month for the third year

*Tenure:*

Initially for 1 year, extendable up to 2 more years or until the completion
of the project (whichever is earlier), subject to performance.

*Age Limit:*

The upper age limit is 35 years. Relaxation will be provided to
SC/ST/OBC/PD candidates as per Government of India rules.

*Last Date to Apply: *5th April 2025

Interested candidates are requested to send their application along with a
detailed CV (including academic mark sheets, publications, awards, research
internships, and GATE/NET scorecard) to the undersigned at
[EMAIL] with the subject line:

“Application for JRF/SRF on TTDF-DoT Project 119”

OR

“Application for JRF/SRF on TTDF-DoT Project 309”

Candidates who prefer to pursue Ph.D. are encouraged to apply against the
above advertisement.
